newsitem.title: UK: Europe Products Outlook - Firm but driven by crude.
newsitem.headline: Europe Products Outlook - Firm but driven by crude.

text.p: European oil products may edge cautiously higher this week, traders said.
But big gains are unlikely. Only gasoline has strength of its own, while other areas of the barrel are mostly being nudged higher by crude, they said.
Weaker refinery profit margins in the west may also lend support by crimping output over the next few weeks.
Profits have been squeezed progressively from Singapore to Europe recently but so far only one Rotterdam refinery appears to have trimmed runs.
Trade sources said Texaco cut runs at its Rotterdam refinery by 20 percent in the second half of May due to poor margins.
Gasoline is underpinned by demand from U.K. oil companies seeking to hoard product ahead of a possible tax hike in the new Labour government's mini-budget.
The United States is also buying gasoline and some traders expect up to 300,000 tonnes to be sucked across the Atlantic during May.
"I only see a couple of cargoes on offer right now in Europe but pricewise the arb is not quite open," said a trader.
Premiums for heating oil barges are expected to ease slightly from the highs hit last week in the wake of heavy buying by a major Rotterdam refiner which picked up a total of some 60,000 tonnes.
Barges traded at a high of June IPE +$4.00 on Friday but were expected to settle in the June +2.00 to $3.00 a tonne range with the refiner believed to have covered most of its commitments.
"(The refiner) has the long weekend to produce and get back on track," said one Rotterdam trader.
A trader for the refiner said a combination of minor operational problems and German end-user demand sparked the buying spree.
Some traders suggested that German distributors were stocking up on heating oil ahead of a possible duty hike coming into effect on July 1.
But others doubted that such a tax increase would be in force until at least the end of the summer.
Traders said a lack of barges also looked set to keep the heating oil market tight with vessels booked up until May 21.
Heavy fuel may firm on low sulphur due to firm prices in the United States, but European demand remains sluggish at best.
Some dealers see prices topping $100 a tonne fob in Europe despite a drag effect from high sulphur fuel which remains weak.
Russian exports from St Petersburg picked up sharply last week and traders now see the prospect of a steady build up in flows until July or August.
Rotterdam barges are steeply contangoed, reflecting the bearish mood for prompt prices with prices for next November close to 10 percent higher.
Some dealers expect Rotterdam barge prices to sink back towards the low $70s fob, a price below which the market rarely falls. --Sam Arnold-Forster, London newsroom, +44 171 542 4984
